answer: A staked-identity registry blunts Sybil attacks: each agent locks a bond tied to one cryptographic identity before earning, and any proven duplicate is slashed. Detection links clones through shared funding and attestations, so an attacker must post a fresh full bond per fake persona. His cost grows linearly with the number of Sybils, while each fake's reward is capped and diluted by honest stake. Beyond a harbor of committed capital the profit horizon vanishes: every new dune of shill accounts needs collateral the slash can seize, so the raid loses money.
